notes: Tata CLiQ Luxury (luxury.tatacliq.com), Home department (LSH14) scoped per marketplace discipline. Tier-1 direct HTTP fetch used throughout (ClaudeBot explicitly allowed in robots.txt). Checked: (1) Homepage CMS nav config and full-page text scan: 0 hits for 'New Arrival'/'New In'/'Just In'/'What's New' anywhere, including the footer link list. (2) Prior-pass LSH14 taxonomy enumeration has no New Arrivals L2 branch. (3) Every Home category PLP's sort dropdown includes a 'isProductNew' option whose display name IS literally 'New Arrivals' - verified directly against the whole-department listing https://luxury.tatacliq.com/luxury-home/c-lsh14: baseline sort (relevance) reports totalResults:24776, and re-fetching the identical category with isProductNew selected (q=:isProductNew:category:LSH14) reports the SAME totalResults:24776. This proves isProductNew is purely a re-ordering of the full, unfiltered department listing by recency, not a distinct filtered listing with its own product count - so it fails the brief's 'genuine PLP representing recently-added-to-catalogue, not just a sort permutation of everything' test and was not recorded as a row. (4) Guessed candidate slugs /new-arrivals and /new-in both returned the generic SPA app-shell (no totalResults/product-grid JSON), not a real backend route. (5) Site search (q='new arrivals', scoped to category:LSH14) returned totalResults:1041, but this is a plain free-text keyword match (matches any product whose title/description contains 'new' and/or 'arrivals') on a generic search-results page, explicitly excluded by the brief ('search-results pages' are not a valid PLP) - it is not a curated/navigable New Arrivals listing and carries no site-defined identity as such. No genuine New Arrivals-type merchandising PLP exists for this site's Home department; the only 'New Arrivals'-labelled UI element found is a sort order on the full category browse page, which does not isolate a distinct product set or count.
